instructions:
OrcaSlicer, a 3D-printing slicer, driven through its GUI.
Workflow: get_state (is it ready? which presets, plates, dialogs?) -> act -> check the result with the reading tools (list_objects, list_plates, get_settings, slice's reply, get_preview); screenshot only to see what they do not report.
- Prefer typed tools (open_files, select_preset, set_settings, slice, export) and run_action (every Speed Dial command: list_actions to search) over GUI clicks.
- What a setting does, or which one controls an effect: get_settings with keys, or query with a few words; each setting's meta has its description and where (its settings page and group).
- For anything else use the GUI tools: ui_snapshot lists widgets, menus, 3D toolbar items, gizmos and ImGui items with refs; ui_click / ui_input / ui_key / ui_mouse act on refs from the latest snapshot.
- Gizmos (Cut, Text, SVG, the painting tools...): ui_click {target: {gizmo: "Cut"}} opens one; its panel's fields and buttons are ImGui items for ui_input / ui_click, and painting is a ui_mouse drag starting on the object. Turn the camera with set_view camera or orbit, never a drag: what a drag does follows the user's mouse settings. gizmo_file only stands in for a file picker inside an open gizmo.
- Objects, parts and plates are 0-based indices, as list_objects and list_plates give them; filament slots and Preview layers are 1-based.
- A call that takes long or opens a dialog returns {status:"running"|"blocked_by_dialog", job}. It keeps running: never retry it. Answer dialogs with dialog_respond (see get_state.dialogs), then wait {for:"job"}. A native message box (native: true) is answered with dialog_respond by one of the buttons listed for it; a file or folder picker, or a native dialog whose buttons list is empty (any on macOS), can't be: register dialog_auto_answer before the step that opens one.
- While an operation (slice, export, arrange or another background job) runs, other changes are refused; use wait or cancel.
- Paths are absolute. Outputs never overwrite an existing file unless overwrite is true.
- screenshot returns a downscaled image plus the full-size PNG path; target "canvas" is the 3D view.
- start_recording / stop_recording record a video (MJPEG .mkv), with the tool calls as captions and the pointer highlighted when captions and pointer ask for them; with encode, stop_recording then encodes it to an MP4 with the system ffmpeg as a job to wait for, and encode_recording encodes any recording later.
- export_script saves this session's calls as a replayable script; run_script replays one.

tools.description: Snapshot of OrcaSlicer: version, platform, whether it is ready, current tab and mode, project, selected printer/process/filament presets, plates, the Preview's view type, time mode and layer range (1-based, with their Z), object count, slicing state, print host uploads (state, progress, error), the open gizmo, open modal dialogs, menus closed unseen (a menu a call opened that no reply listed), notifications, running jobs and a running recording. Call it first and whenever you are unsure what the app is doing.
tools.name: get_state
tools.title: Get app state

tools.description: Block until a condition holds or timeout_s passes (max 50). for: "ready" (startup finished), "idle" (no dialog, no running job, nothing slicing or arranging, no gizmo working in the background), "dialog" / "no_dialog", or "job" with a job id returned by an earlier call - then the reply is that job's result. Returns {satisfied:false} on timeout; call it again.

for.description: What to wait for; default job when job is given, else idle.

tools.name: wait
tools.title: Wait for a condition

tools.description: The last lines of OrcaSlicer's current log file, optionally only those at or above a level.
tools.name: get_log
tools.title: Read the log

tools.description: Search everything the Speed Dial can run: built-in commands (slice, export, views, object operations, plates, calibration wizards, help), recent projects, plugin scripts and pages. Each entry has an id for run_action, a description and, when it takes one, a param (type and help). include_settings also lists settings (each jumps to that setting in the sidebar; use get_settings / set_settings to read or change values).

query.description: Case-insensitive text to find in id, title, group or description.

tools.name: list_actions
tools.title: Search Speed Dial actions

tools.description: Run one action by the id list_actions returned (orca_command:view_front:orca, or the name inside it, view_front), with its param when it takes one (a percent, tab id, plate index, or an absolute path - commands with a path parameter skip their file dialog; outputs need {"path": ..., "overwrite": true} to replace a file). Actions that open a dialog return blocked_by_dialog; answer it with dialog_respond, or, for a native one it can't press (a file picker), register dialog_auto_answer before the call. An export_gcode with a path completes when the file is written; an action that starts a background job (obj_arrange, obj_orient) when the job ends. An action that does nothing (no object selected) is an error. Some commands add what they did to the reply (the obj_order_by_* order, the object obj_assemble made).

id.description: Action id from list_actions, or the name inside it.

param.description: Parameter, when the action takes one.

tools.name: run_action
tools.title: Run a Speed Dial action

tools.description: Open model files (STL, 3MF, STEP, OBJ, AMF, SVG...), a project (.3mf) or G-code by absolute path, without a file dialog. Models are added to the current project. A .3mf opens as a project (replacing the current one: pass discard_changes when it has unsaved changes) unless as is "geometry". Importing can open a dialog (STEP mesh options, for instance); the reply is then blocked_by_dialog.

as.description: How to open .3mf files. Default auto (= project).

discard_changes.description: Replace a project with unsaved changes without asking.

tools.name: open_files
tools.title: Open files

tools.description: Start a new, empty project. Fails when the current project has unsaved changes unless discard_changes is true. Modified printer, process and filament presets are kept for the new project, unless changes is "discard", the two answers of New Project's prompt. Reply: objects, names, plates; when presets had or have unsaved changes, discarded and modified list per preset the keys dropped and the keys still unsaved.

changes.description: Unsaved changes of the presets: keep them (default) or drop them.

tools.name: new_project
tools.title: New project

tools.description: Generate a Calibration menu test as its dialog's OK does: a new project named after the test with the test model, and the process, filament and printer presets changed as the test needs (presets_changed). The test prints with filament slot 1, so the filament tab is pointed at slot 1's preset. Omitted parameters take the dialog's defaults (pressure advance's by the printer's extruder type); temperatures are clamped to 155-500 °C and rounded down to 5 °C. Fails, changing nothing, when the project has unsaved changes (pass discard_changes) or presets do (pass changes). Reply: test, project, params (the values used, which the journal records), objects, names, plates, presets_changed, result_keys (where the measured value belongs), warnings, adjusted (vfa), and discarded and modified as new_project. Then slice and export. To save a measured value: new_project {discard_changes, changes: "discard"}, set_settings the value, save_preset.

accelerations.description: pressure_advance pattern: one test per acceleration and speed; default the process's.

auto_adjust.description: vfa: lower the layer height, else the end speed, to stay within the filament's maximum volumetric speed (default true).

auto_scale.description: temperature, vfa: scale the model to the nozzle (default true).

changes.description: Unsaved preset changes: keep them for the test, or drop them first. Required when presets are modified.

damping.description: input_shaping_freq: the damping ratio printed with.

discard_changes.description: Replace a project with unsaved changes.

end_y.description: input_shaping_freq: end of the Y range; default the X one.

freq_y.description: input_shaping_damp: the Y frequency, Hz; default freq_x.

method.description: pressure_advance: tower (default), line or pattern; flow_ratio: pass1, pass2, yolo (default) or yolo_perfectionist.

print_numbers.description: pressure_advance line: print the values (default true).

shaper_type.description: Input shaping: an input_shaping_type the printer's firmware offers; default the first.

speeds.description: pressure_advance pattern: default an optimal speed.

start.description: Start of the swept value: °C, mm³/s, PA, mm, mm/s (vfa), Hz (input_shaping_freq), damping (input_shaping_damp), junction deviation mm or jerk mm/s (cornering).

start_y.description: input_shaping_freq: start of the Y range; default the X one.

test.description: The test, named as the calib_* actions.

test_model.description: Input shaping: ringing_tower (default) or fast_tower; cornering: also scv_v2; temperature on belt printers: standard (default) or overhang.

tools.name: calibrate
tools.title: Generate a calibration test

tools.description: Save the project as a .3mf at an absolute path without a dialog; it becomes the project's file.
tools.name: save_project
tools.title: Save the project

tools.description: Write the project to a file without a dialog. gcode: the current plate's G-code (slice first; runs in the background and the call completes when the file is written). sliced_3mf: the sliced plate (or all plates) as .gcode.3mf. 3mf: the model without slicing data. stl: all objects as one STL. Without format, the path's extension (.gcode, .gcode.3mf, .3mf, .stl) says which. plate selects the plate first.

format.description: What to write; default from the path's extension.

tools.name: export
tools.title: Export

tools.description: Printer, process or filament presets with flags: system or user, selected (and modified), compatible with the selected printer, and for filaments the slots using them. Only compatible, visible presets unless asked.

include_incompatible.description: Also list presets incompatible with the printer.

tools.name: list_presets
tools.title: List presets

tools.description: Select a printer, process or filament preset by the name its selector shows (or its internal name), as a person would. With unsaved changes the Transfer-or-discard prompt opens (blocked_by_dialog) unless changes answers it. A filament is assigned to filament_slot (1-based, default 1). Reply: selected; when presets had or have unsaved changes, discarded and modified list per preset the keys dropped and the keys still unsaved.

changes.description: Unsaved changes of the presets the switch replaces: move them to the new preset or drop them, as the prompt's buttons do. Omitted: the prompt opens.

name.description: Preset name as list_presets shows it.

tools.name: select_preset
tools.title: Select a preset

tools.description: Save the printer, process or filament preset being edited, unsaved changes included, under name, as the tab's Save and the Save preset dialog's OK do; it is then selected. A filament is filament_slot's (default 1), and every slot using the old preset takes the new one. Replacing another existing preset needs overwrite (pass it in scripts meant to be rerun). Reply: saved, user, project, inherits, filament_slots. A temperature warning or an unsaved-changes prompt makes it blocked_by_dialog. To keep only some edits, set_settings {reset_all: true, values} first.

detach.description: Copy inherited values and drop the parent (Developer mode).

inside_project.description: Keep it inside the project, not as a user preset. Default: where the edited preset is.

overwrite.description: Replace another preset of that name.

tools.name: save_preset
tools.title: Save a preset

tools.description: Delete a user preset or one inside the project, its file and its cloud copy, as the tab's Delete does, without asking. A selected preset is replaced as the tab does (its parent or the next preset). Another filament is deleted without changing the selection, and slots using it take the selected one; another process is selected, deleted and the selection restored; a printer must be selected first. Refused: system presets, presets others inherit from, another preset while the edited one of its type has unsaved changes. Deleting a selected printer or process can ask about other presets' unsaved changes (blocked_by_dialog). Reply: deleted, selected, filaments (per slot), attached, and discarded/modified as select_preset's.

delete_attached.description: A custom printer: also delete the process and filament presets made for it alone, which the GUI deletes with it.

name.description: Preset name as list_presets shows it.

tools.name: delete_preset
tools.title: Delete a preset

tools.description: Read setting values (as OrcaSlicer serializes them) with meta: label, description (what the setting does, when to change it, what it affects), where (its settings page and group), type, unit, range, allowed values and their labels, and mode. Name keys; find the settings for an effect with query, a few words matched in keys, labels and descriptions, best matches first; or list one page or group with where (an unknown one lists them all). Without these, every option of the scope is listed, paged, without meta in a preset scope. A per-variant value lists in meta its variants (what each entry is for) and active (the entry each extruder prints with). preset reads a saved preset without selecting it; compare lists only the keys that differ from another preset, each with value and other. For object/volume scopes only the overrides that object or part carries are listed, each with effective (the value it prints with) and source (part, object, process or default); an object's item lists in parts the parts and modifiers that override the key inside their own volume. The project scope has the plate type, slot colours, flushing volumes, purge mode, prime tower position per plate, which slots are mixed and, with several extruders, the filament grouping; meta.offered lists the choices this printer has. The plate scope lists a plate's curr_bed_type, print_sequence, spiral_mode, first_layer_print_sequence, other_layers_print_sequence, name and locked, each with value (the plate's own, null where it follows the global setting or Auto) and effective. The preferences scope reads the named keys of the app configuration (the Preferences dialog's settings, keys as its controls are named), values as stored, and lists no keys unasked.

compare.description: Preset scopes: a preset name, ":saved" (the unsaved changes) or ":parent" (the preset it inherits from).

include_meta.description: Include labels, types and ranges. Default true, false for a preset scope's whole listing and with compare.

plate.description: Plate index (plate scope; default: the current plate).

preset.description: Preset scopes: read this saved preset (a name from list_presets) instead of the one being edited.

query.description: A few distinctive words, e.g. "stringing" or "ooze travel"; the best 20 matches unless limit says otherwise.

scope.description: Which settings: the process (print), filament or printer preset being edited, an object's / part's own overrides, the project's own settings, a plate's, or the app's preferences (read only).

where.description: A settings page, or "Page > Group" as meta.where gives it, e.g. "Strength > Walls".

tools.name: get_settings
tools.title: Read settings

tools.description: Change settings as if typed into the settings tab: all values are parsed strictly first and applied together, and nothing changes if any is invalid. Values may be strings in OrcaSlicer's format ("15%", "0.2", "1,2") or JSON numbers, booleans and arrays (a point as [x, y]). object/volume scopes set per-object or per-part overrides, of the keys the object list offers there; a null value removes an override. extruder is the object's or part's filament (1-based; 0 or null is Default), set as the Change Filament menu does. A preset's per-variant value (get_settings meta.variants) takes a single value for the entries in use (meta.active, as the tab writes the variant it shows), {"index": i, "value": v} for one entry, or an array of all. In a preset scope, null takes a key back to its saved value (reset_to parent: the parent's), and reset_all first discards every unsaved change, as the tab's undo button does (reply: reverted), then applies values. Reply: applied, and changed, every setting the call changed, including those the app adjusted in turn. Spiral vase and some others confirm their adjustments in a dialog (blocked_by_dialog). The project scope writes as the sidebar's controls do: curr_bed_type, filament_colour (#RRGGBB per slot), flush_multiplier, flush_volumes_matrix (per nozzle, slots x slots from row to column, in config order over every slot, mixed ones left as they are; before the multiplier, which the G-code header applies; a colour change can recalculate it, so set it last), prime_volume_mode, and wipe_tower_x/y (mm from the plate's origin, one per plate; undoable). The plate scope writes as the Plate Settings dialog's OK does, after selecting the plate as its icon does: curr_bed_type, print_sequence ("by layer", "by object"), spiral_mode (true asks for confirmation: blocked_by_dialog), first_layer_print_sequence (every slot once, e.g. [2, 1]) and other_layers_print_sequence ([{from: layer >= 2, to, order}], to omitted for the last layer), null for the global setting or Auto; name, and locked (true or false). One undo step.

plate.description: Plate index (plate scope; default: the current plate).

reset_all.description: Preset scopes: discard the unsaved changes before applying values.

reset_to.description: Preset scopes: what a null value takes a key back to: the saved preset (default) or the preset it inherits from.

scope.description: Which settings: the process (print), filament or printer preset being edited, an object's / part's own overrides, the project's own settings, a plate's, or the app's preferences (read only).

values.description: {key: value}, or {key: {index, value}} for one entry

tools.name: set_settings
tools.title: Change settings

tools.description: Plates with name, locked, current, objects ([object, instance]), and the settings they print with: curr_bed_type, print_sequence, spiral_mode, first_layer_print_sequence and other_layers_print_sequence (null: Auto); overrides lists those the plate sets itself (set_settings scope plate). Also sliced (an up-to-date slice), wipe_tower [x, y] and layer_gcode: the plate's pauses, custom G-code, templates and filament changes, each {z, layer, type, filament, color, gcode}; layer is the Preview slider's number, given while the plate's slice is up to date.
tools.name: list_plates
tools.title: List plates

tools.description: Objects in the project: filament, auto_drop, bounding box (instance 0), brim ear count and the settings they override; their instances (plate, offset, rotation in degrees, scale, mirrored, bbox); their parts and modifiers (type, with subtype for a precise seam; filament: a part's own or its object's, a modifier's only when it sets one; position, bbox and scaled_volume in mm3 on the bed, measured on instance 0; rotation_deg and scale in the object's frame; mirrored; triangle count; mesh_volume, the unscaled mesh's mm3; painted facets: supports and seam enforcers/blockers, fuzzy_skin, mmu per filament, texture per layer; a text part's text and font, an SVG part's file); its height range modifiers when it has any (layer_config_ranges: [{min_z, max_z, values}], as set_layer_ranges takes them) and its variable layer height profile when it has one (layer_height_profile: {points, min_height, max_height}). A bbox is {min, max, size} in mm of model parts only, so unlike the panel's Size it leaves out modifiers. Indices are what select, transform, ui_mouse targets and the object/volume settings scopes take.

screen.description: Add each instance's rectangle in the shown 3D view, logical pixels [x, y, w, h].

tools.name: list_objects
tools.title: List objects

tools.description: Select objects, instances or parts in the 3D view (the assemble view while it is shown, else Prepare, switching to it), as clicking them would. Give objects, instances ([[object, instance], ...]) or volumes ([[object, part], ...]); add keeps the current selection; all / none select everything or nothing.

add.description: Add to the selection instead of replacing it.

tools.name: select
tools.title: Select objects

annotations.title: Move, rotate or scale an instance or a part

tools.description: Change one instance's placement, or one part's with volume. translate is in mm, position where it goes (mm, as the Move panel shows it, whatever mode says), rotate in degrees about X/Y/Z, scale a factor (one number or [x, y, z]), size [x, y, z] mm along the object's or part's own axes, plate moves the instance onto that plate at the same place. mode "relative" (default) adds to the current placement, "absolute" sets it. An instance is dropped back onto the bed unless drop_to_bed is false. A part moves as the Object manipulation panel moves it: translate and rotate along the bed's axes, measured on instance 0, scale and size along its own axes; every instance shows the change, and Auto Drop may lower the object afterwards. One undo step. Replies with the instance's offset, scale and plate, or the part's size along its own axes and its list_objects entry (volume_info).

plate.description: Move the instance to this plate.

position.description: [x, y, z] mm: the position to move to. Not with translate.

rotate.description: [x, y, z] degrees; relative only for a part

size.description: [x, y, z] mm, null keeps an axis; one number and two nulls keep the proportions. Not with scale.

volume.description: Transform this part instead of the instance.

tools.name: transform
tools.title: Move, rotate or scale an instance or a part

annotations.title: Add a part or modifier to an object

tools.description: Add a part, negative part, modifier, support blocker or enforcer, or precise seam to an object, as its context menu's Add items do: a primitive shape at a size, or a model file as Load... adds it. The part lands where the menu puts it (a shape beside the object, a file at its coordinates relative to the object's first part) unless position is given. Like the menu, adding a shape folds the instance's rotation and scale into the object's parts (the instance's scale then reads 1). Refused for an object with several instances: add parts first. A STEP file may ask for mesh options (blocked_by_dialog). The new part is selected; one undo step. Replies with its index, which is not always the last (parts are ordered by type), the object's part count and the part's list_objects entry (volume_info).

path.description: Instead of shape: absolute path of a model file (STL, OBJ, 3MF, STEP, ...).

position.description: [x, y, z] mm on the bed for the part's centre, on instance 0, as the Move panel shows it.

size.description: mm, the Primitive size dialog's fields: cube [x, y, z]; cylinder, cone, disc [diameter, height]; sphere [diameter]; torus [inner diameter, tube diameter]. Default: the built-in size.

tools.name: add_part
tools.title: Add a part or modifier to an object

annotations.title: Arrange objects or fill the bed

tools.description: Arrange objects as the toolbar's Arrange does (every unlocked plate) or as one plate's Arrange icon does (plates: an index or "current"), or fill object fill's plate with more of it, as Fill bed with instances or copies does. spacing, rotate, align_y and multi_material are the Arrange options panel's settings: values given are kept as the panel keeps them, so later arranges use them too. Waits for the arrangement (a longer one replies with a job); the reply has the settings in force, instances left off every plate, plates the all-plates arrange skipped and the job's notifications. An arrange may reorder objects, so list_objects again. One undo step.

align_y.description: Align to Y axis (off while rotate is on).

fill.description: Instead of arranging, fill this object's plate with more of it.

multi_material.description: Allow multiple materials on same plate.

tools.name: arrange
tools.title: Arrange objects or fill the bed

tools.description: Slice the current plate, all plates, or one plate by index, the way the toolbar's Slice button does, and wait for the result (or reply with a job id when it takes longer than the reply budget). Each requested plate reports ok, error, cancelled, empty or skipped; the whole operation is superseded when someone else started a slice or edited the project while it ran. An ok plate has time_s (silent_time_s when the printer estimates it), filament_m and filament_g including flush, filament_cost, layers, max_z, filament_changes, and filaments[i] for slot i+1 with m, g and the grams of model_g, support_g, flush_g and tower_g. Other changes are refused until it finishes; cancel stops it.
tools.name: slice
tools.title: Slice

tools.description: Stop the running slice or G-code export, as the cancel button on the slicing progress does, or the background job (an arrange, orient or fill bed) an MCP call started. That job then reports cancelled; a background job keeps other changes out until it has really stopped. With job, only when that job is the running operation, or a running encode_recording, which stops and reports cancelled. Allowed while an operation holds the project.

job.description: The operation's job to cancel, e.g. "j12".

tools.name: cancel
tools.title: Cancel an operation

tools.description: Replace an object's height range modifiers (Height Range Modifier in the object list): Z ranges in mm, each printed with its own layer_height, filament and process settings, starting from the object's layer height and filament. Ranges may touch but not overlap; [] removes them all. One undo step; the object is selected. Replies with the object's height and its ranges as list_objects shows them, and warnings, such as a variable layer height profile deciding the layer heights instead.

layer_config_ranges.description: The object's ranges afterwards, in any order.

values.description: {key: value} as set_settings takes them: layer_height, extruder (0 = the object's filament) and per-region process settings such as sparse_infill_density or wall_loops.

tools.name: set_layer_ranges
tools.title: Set height range modifiers

annotations.title: Set a variable layer height profile

tools.description: Run the Variable layer height panel's Adaptive, Smooth or Reset on an object, without opening the panel: adaptive computes layer heights from the object's shape (inside a height range, the range's layer_height), smooth smooths its profile (or the one its height ranges give), reset goes back to its layer height and ranges. One undo step; the object is selected. Replies with the object's height, its layer_height_profile {points, min_height, max_height} as list_objects shows it (absent after reset), and warnings.

keep_min.description: smooth: keep the minimum layer heights (default false).

quality.description: adaptive: 0 = quality .. 1 = speed (default 0.5, as the panel).

tools.name: set_layer_height_profile
tools.title: Set a variable layer height profile

tools.description: Add or remove pauses, custom G-code, custom templates and filament changes at the start of a layer, as the Preview layer slider's menu does; they are saved per plate in the project. They go on the plate's sliced layers, so the plate needs an up-to-date slice, or must be the one the Preview still shows after an earlier edit; the call selects it and shows the Preview. Applies clear, then remove, then add, all checked first. One code per layer: a custom code or filament change where there is one replaces it. Not undoable, as in the slider. A change invalidates the plate's slice: slice again before exporting. Replies with the plate's codes as list_plates' layer_gcode lists them, each with z and layer.

add.description: Codes to add, each with layer or z.

filament.description: change_filament: printed from this layer up.

layer.description: 1-based, as the Preview's layer slider numbers layers.

z.description: mm: the layer whose top is at or above it.

clear.description: Remove every code on the plate first.

remove.description: Codes to remove, by layer or z.

layer.description: 1-based, as the Preview's layer slider numbers layers.

z.description: mm: the layer whose top is at or above it.

tools.name: set_layer_gcode
tools.title: Set layer G-codes

tools.description: Capture what OrcaSlicer shows and return it as an image, downscaled to max_dim on the long edge (default 1280), plus the full-size PNG written to save_path (or the session's output folder). target: "window" (the main window), "canvas" (the visible 3D view exactly as rendered: scene, toolpaths, toolbars, ImGui panels; on the Design tab its view), "dialog" (the topmost modal dialog), or a widget's ref from ui_snapshot (a window that is not modal, or just that widget; a page element's ref captures its whole web view). The result says when parts may differ from the screen (approximate). Point the view first with set_view.

include_image.description: Return the image itself (default true); false returns only the path.

max_dim.description: Long edge of the returned image.

save_path.description: Absolute .png path for the full-size image.

target.description: window (default), canvas, dialog, or a widget's ref or locator from ui_snapshot.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.title: Take a screenshot

tools.description: What the Preview shows for a sliced plate. summary: the slice reply's, plus prepare and travel time and travel distance. features: seconds, share of the print time and grams per feature type (the Line Type legend), and travel. layers: per layer (1-based, as set_view's layer) Z, height, seconds and grams, paged; layer_features adds each feature type's seconds. objects: grams per object instance, with its list_objects index when its name is unique. view, for the plate the Preview shows: view type, time mode, layer range, which legend rows are visible, and each view type's colour range for what the legend shows. Times are normal-mode estimates. A G-code file opened for viewing reads the same.

plate.description: Plate index; default the current plate.

tools.name: get_preview
tools.title: Read the Preview

tools.description: Set up what the window shows, for screenshots and GUI work: the main tab, the 3D view (Prepare's, the preview or the assemble view, which has its own gizmos), the 3D camera (a named direction, the default view, or fit to bed / objects / selection, then orbit to look from between the named directions; the reply gives the elevation and azimuth it ends at), the preview's color scheme (picked as in the legend's combo, which shows every feature type again), legend rows, time estimate and layers (1-based, or up to a height), and the window size. Only the given fields change. On the Design tab the camera points its view (default is its Home view; no fit_bed). A menu a right click opens is listed as popup_menu, or popup_item (with click or up) runs one of its items. camera_moved in the reply says the gesture moved the camera, so earlier screenshots and pixels no longer match the view. tools.description: Record a video of OrcaSlicer until stop_recording: the main window with any modal dialog on it (target window), or the 3D view shown (canvas). Frames are MJPEG in a Matroska (.mkv) file with their real timestamps. With captions, the tool call acting on the app shows as a caption at the bottom (secret setting values never show); with pointer, the pointer is highlighted, its clicks rippling. Capture takes at most about a third of the UI thread, so the frame rate drops where capturing is slow. One recording at a time: one a script starts ends with the script, a client's when the server is turned off. With encode, the stop_recording that reports it also encodes it to an MP4 beside it, as the Start Recording command does; encode_recording makes an MP4 of any recording later.

tools.description: Bring the project in line with a printer, as the sidebar's "Sync printer information" and "Sync AMS" do. Step 1 (include_nozzles, default true): per extruder nozzle diameter (switching the printer preset to the one for that diameter) and flow type, the number of AMS units per extruder, and the filament switch flags. Step 2: the project's filaments take the presets, colours and types of the printer's AMS trays and external spools (mode "override": the filaments are replaced by the trays in order; color_only keeps the presets and only copies colours). The printer is selected first and its state awaited. dry_run returns the planned changes ({nozzles, ams_counts, filaments}) and changes nothing; the AMS part lists which preset each tray selects (unknown filaments fall back to a generic preset, decided when the sync runs). Printers that hold several nozzles per extruder (hotend rack) are refused in step 1: their nozzle picker is a dialog. May raise the dialogs of the GUI (unsaved preset changes).

color_only.description: Only copy tray colours into the project; keep its filament presets (default false).

dry_run.description: Build and return exactly what would be sent to the printer, and send nothing. Bambu Lab printers only.

include_nozzles.description: Also sync nozzle diameters, flow types and AMS counts (default true).

tools.description: Send a sliced plate to a printer and start the print, as the Print dialog's Send does. Runs the same plan as print_plan (same arguments: plate, overrides, options) and refuses with the blocking errors in details when it is not sendable; warnings the dialog confirms in a popup (plan needs_confirmation) refuse the call unless confirm_warnings is true. The plate is selected, its sliced 3mf (and for cloud printers its config 3mf) exported like Plater::send_gcode, and the job runs on a worker: on a hotend-rack printer the printer is first asked for a fresh nozzle mapping (up to 10 s). With the timelapse option on, the printer's storage is checked first as the dialog does; when it is low the call refuses until confirm_timelapse_storage is true (the oldest timelapse videos are then deleted), or options.timelapse is false. dry_run builds the plan and the PrintParams the job would send (secrets redacted) and sends nothing: no file is exported, no job is created and the current plate stays. A dry run returns {sendable, errors, warnings, plan, print_params, files} even when the plan is blocked; a real run refuses. Real runs return {started, message}; the Monitor tab is shown afterwards as in the dialog. plate is the 0-based plate index. A LAN printer that rejects the access code or address fails the call instead of opening the dialog's address prompt.

confirm_timelapse_storage.description: Allow deleting the oldest timelapse videos when the timelapse storage is low.

tools.description: Heat, fans, speed, light and motion on the selected (or dev_id) Bambu printer, as the Device tab does. Actions: set_temp {target: nozzle|bed|chamber, value C (0 = off), extruder? Temperatures, fans, speed and the light work during a print; home, jog, extrude and select_extruder are refused while printing. tools.description: Call a method of the Design (CAD) tab's control surface. Method "describe_tools" lists the methods and their params; narrow it with params {"method": name or [names]} or {"query": text}. Typical calls: describe_scene, describe_feature / set_feature (read and edit a feature as its card does), sketch_begin / sketch_add (entities, polygon, slot, ellipse, spline) / sketch_commit then extrude or revolve {sketch}; in the sketch, sketch_fillet, sketch_trim, sketch_transform (move, rotate, array) and sketch_constrain / sketch_constraints; hole, thread, sweep (along a sketch or helix), loft, split {plane}, fillet, boolean, plane (datum), query_topology (face kinds, adjacency, filters), measure (min_distance), commit (Commit to Plate), undo / redo (the Design history; run_action undo is Prepare's). A method that fails is an error and leaves the design as it was; the older ones in describe_tools' legacy_ok_false answer ok false instead. thread, sweep and loft can take seconds, and their reply may be a job. Pass the "generation" from describe_scene or query_topology with face and edge ids so ids read before the model changed are refused. Needs the CAD feature enabled in Preferences (it takes effect after a restart).
